I verified those three forbidden directions are currently accepted.

4. **Operational and ownership docs retain obsolete names.** [Account setup commands](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/services/account/README.md:91) still use `nucleus-app`, `memotron-app`, and `pointron-app`; all three selectors fail. content.text:
**Mostly yes for the client’s structure, but a few details are inaccurate, and the map is not a complete picture of the system’s dependencies.**

The dependency-map table exactly matches the enforced matrix. All 146 public feature entries match package exports, and recorded current package names match manifests. Fresh checks passed: **11,554 resolved imports, zero architecture violations**, and all **383 type dispositions**.

These documentation leftovers remain:

| Issue | Correction needed |
|---|---|
| Both ownership docs say “the checker wins.” | Limit that to enforced import policy. The constitution and semantic ownership rules remain authoritative; the checker cannot establish correct ownership. |
| [Client boundaries](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md:76) says stories are excluded. | The architecture gate includes 27 story files. Only the workspace-dependency check excludes stories. |
| [Type ownership](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/type-ownership.md:51) says every server-to-client import is rejected. | Tests are excluded from that boundary rule; several server tests still import client Resource definitions. |
| UI environment is described as viewport/presentation measurements. | It also owns portable platform, appearance, debug, logging, haptic and asset-resolution contracts. The UI README’s blanket prohibition on stores needs the same qualification. |
| [The component chain](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/docs/architecture/client-dependency-map.md:160) says overlays, shortcuts and Intercom mount after loading. | Overlays and shortcuts require only `isBaseLoaded`; Intercom is outside the loading gate. |

The feature and shared-state READMEs also omit permitted dependencies while describing their lists as exhaustive.

**I think the architecture’s direction is good.** Portable UI, named state owners, cross-feature surfaces, a separate shell, and a narrow composition root give the code understandable homes. Host contracts and injected chrome successfully remove upward imports. I would keep this structure.

The next improvements should address these concrete weaknesses:

- **Finish semantic ownership cleanup.** [App context](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts:22) still owns calendar selection (`selectedTimePeriod`), support configuration (`intercomId`), and a separate touch-device store populated by calendar code. `leftThresholdCrossedStore` has no callers. These belong with their existing semantic owners or should be removed when unused.
- **Reduce state-module cycles.** I found five cycle groups among value imports. Prioritize navigation↔tabs and analytics store↔analytics helpers. Recursive Markdown rendering may be intentional and deserves separate treatment.
- **Distinguish owner, workspace and observed graphs.** The permitted owner graph is acyclic, but `@nucleum/client` has mutual manifest dependencies with seven client packages, partly through peers. The current map documents its exclusion, but readers should not infer that the workspace graph is also acyclic.
- **Make host lifetime explicit.** Registration currently happens through module-import side effects, including an undisposed context subscription. Explicit installation and disposal would make isolated mounts, tests and reloads easier to reason about.
- **Generate the dependency table and add a system data-flow diagram.** Keep ownership prose handwritten. Add the client DataFn → account service → database/search/lookup paths, with legacy persistence and recovery boundaries.

The earlier Settings findings also remain documented: modal selection dismisses the overlay, and constrained landscape panels suppress detail content. The relevant source conditions remain; I did not repeat browser QA during this audit.

My priority order would be **documentation accuracy, semantic ownership leftovers, state cycles, then lifecycle and graph tooling**. This audit was read-only.
